# Ospia

> Ospia is an AI-native Hospital Operating System for Indian hospitals: a digital
> workforce of AI agents that runs admissions, billing, claims, pharmacy and
> inventory alongside hospital staff, under an autonomy level the hospital sets
> per task, with every decision explainable and replayable.

Ospia is early. We work with design-partner hospitals and do not publish customer
counts or outcome figures we have not earned.

## Start here

- [What is an AI Hospital Operating System? | Ospia](https://ospia.in/ai-hospital-operating-system.html): An AI-native Hospital Operating System runs a hospital's clinical, financial and operational work through governed AI agents on one unified database. What it is, how it differs from a legacy HIS/HMS, and why Indian hospitals need one.
- [Platform — Ospia Hospital Operating System](https://ospia.in/platform.html): The Ospia platform: ten capability pillars, the task and intent registry, the rules and policy engine, permanent event history and the insight surface.
- [AI Workforce — twelve digital employees | Ospia](https://ospia.in/ai-workforce.html): Ospia's AI workforce: twelve digital employees with defined responsibilities, permissions, KPIs and escalation rules — each at an autonomy level the hospital configures from L0 to L4.
- [Architecture — Ospia Hospital Operating System](https://ospia.in/architecture.html): Ospia's architecture: a modular monolith with fully isolated domains, per-module schemas, a durable event backbone, and six CI-enforced architectural gates.
- [Compliance — ABDM, DPDP, NMC, NABH, GST | Ospia](https://ospia.in/compliance.html): How Ospia meets Indian healthcare regulation: ABDM and ABHA, DPDP consent ledger, NMC prescribing rules enforced at write time, NABH evidence, GST e-invoicing, plus HIPAA readiness and ISO roadmap.
- [Security — Ospia Hospital Operating System](https://ospia.in/security.html): Ospia security in detail: zero trust, multi-tenancy and data isolation, encryption, key management, hash-chained audit, backup and disaster recovery, secure SDLC, penetration testing and the compliance roadmap.

## Insights

- [Compliant by design: ABDM, DPDP, NMC and GST, enforced at write-time](https://ospia.in/insights/compliant-by-design.html): ABDM, DPDP, NMC and GST shouldn't be a document you produce at audit time. Compliant-by-design means the regulation is built into the data model and enforced at write-time — so an Indian hospital stays audit-ready continuously.
- [Credit note reconciliation: where hospital finance quietly leaks](https://ospia.in/insights/credit-note-reconciliation-where-hospital-finance-quietly-leaks.html): A CFO’s guide to closing the loop on hospital credit notes—without new software—and how Ospia fits when you’re ready.
- [HMS timelines: why they stretch into years — and how to shorten them](https://ospia.in/insights/hms-timelines-why-they-stretch-into-years-and-how-to-shorten-them.html): The mechanism behind HMS overruns, what to do before you buy, and the gated implementation model Ospia uses to keep time and scope honest.
- [How to govern AI agents in a hospital like new hires](https://ospia.in/insights/how-to-govern-ai-agents-in-a-hospital-like-new-hires.html): A practical governance model for AI in Indian hospitals: scope, permissions, KPIs, escalation and audit — and where Ospia fits.
- [Migrating off your old HMS without the horror story](https://ospia.in/insights/migration-without-the-horror.html): The fear of migrating off an old hospital system keeps hospitals stuck on software they have outgrown. Parallel running, verification and a real rollback path turn migration from a leap of faith into a controlled cutover.
- [NABH software requirements — a plain‑language explainer for medical directors](https://ospia.in/insights/nabh-software-requirements-a-plain-language-explainer-for-medical-dire.html): What NABH actually needs from your systems, why audits feel like fire drills, what to fix without buying anything, and where Ospia fits.
- [You don't need a new HMS. You need to stop buying HMS.](https://ospia.in/insights/stop-buying-hms.html): Why hospitals keep buying the wrong thing: the replacement, integration and coordination taxes baked into the HMS model — and why an AI Hospital Operating System ends the replace-every-five-years ritual.
- [The revenue your hospital is quietly losing — and how to stop it](https://ospia.in/insights/stop-the-leakage.html): Hospitals lose real revenue to charges that were delivered but never captured and to claims rejected after submission. An AI Hospital Operating System catches leakage before it happens — the digital workforce reconciles the day.
- [The real cost components of hospital software in India](https://ospia.in/insights/the-real-cost-components-of-hospital-software-in-india.html): Licence is not your biggest line item. How Indian hospitals can model true TCO of their HMS over seven years—and what changes if you choose an operating system.
- [Every vendor says 'AI-powered.' Three questions that end the conversation.](https://ospia.in/insights/three-questions.html): Every hospital software vendor claims to be AI-powered. Three questions — decision replay, configurable autonomy, and provider-independence — separate a governed AI operating system from an AI feature stapled onto old architecture.
- [The nine reasons Indian TPAs reject claims, ranked by how often](https://ospia.in/insights/tpa-claim-rejection-reasons.html): Nine common, preventable reasons TPAs reject or short-pay hospital claims in India, ordered as a practical pre-submission checklist.
- [Weeks, not years: why implementation stops being a five-year project](https://ospia.in/insights/weeks-not-years.html): Traditional hospital software takes years to implement because it is customised, not configured. An AI Hospital Operating System goes live in weeks because the capabilities already exist and you configure them to your hospital.
- [What is a Hospital Operating System? The short version](https://ospia.in/insights/what-is-a-hospital-operating-system-the-short-version.html): Why hospitals keep replacing HMS, what a Hospital Operating System is, and how Ospia’s autonomy and governance model changes what you control.
- [What NABH actually requires from your software, clause by clause](https://ospia.in/insights/what-nabh-actually-requires-from-your-software-clause-by-clause.html): NABH does not test your software directly — it tests whether your processes leave a trace. Clause by clause, what an assessor actually asks for, and where hospital systems built to transact rather than to prove fall short.
